steps.cap: A photomask is the stencil that lithography prints from, at least one for each layer of a chip. Inside the scanner, light bounces off the mask and carries its pattern down to the wafer.
No glass lets extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light through. So the mask for EUV layers is a mirror, built up from about forty pairs of very thin layers laid on glass, and the light bounces off it.
A dark pattern drawn on the mirror soaks up the light wherever no line should print. The light that bounces back carries the pattern of one layer.
The same mask prints its layer on wafer after wafer, so one plate shapes millions of chips.

A speck of dust on the mask prints on every wafer, until someone finds it. So a thin membrane on a frame, called a pellicle, covers the mask's patterned side and catches dust where it is too far out of focus to print.
